meta.tileset: Dungeon Crawl Stone Soup tiles, Oct 5 2010 (CC0)
meta.credit: Tiles by the Dungeon Crawl Stone Soup team and rltiles contributors, released under CC0. Chain and rail sprites derived from an asset pack by MidnitePixel.
meta.note: Keys are tile ids from tiles.json. `sprite` is one image; `frames` animates; `text` is drawn by the font layer instead of the atlas.
meta.localAssets: Sprites under local/ come from port/assets/. The chains and rail are cut from a Castlevania asset pack by MidnitePixel (itch.io), used with the author's permission for any purpose, with credit. The gems are generated.

0.comment: floor, only drawn when a level sets MakeFloor

4.comment: Block, MBlock and ZBlock are all col(6,7) brown glyph 178 in the original -- indistinguishable, so which one a spell will break is not given away.

7.comment: A closed chest -- it is closed until you walk into it.

9.comment: New_Gem_Color re-rolls the gem colour on entering each level, any CGA colour but 8. Drawn as CP437 4, the diamond suit.

12.comment: An actual key; the rune stand-in read as nothing in particular.

19.comment: Forest: a solid green mass in the original (#219 in green). Always falls to one whip crack, so it must read as clearly different from a Tree.

20.comment: Tree: an individual tree (CP437 club), resists the whip at random(7) < WhipPower.

21.comment: no bomb in Crawl; orb stands in

23.comment: A pit is instant death, so it must never blend into the background. The original drew it as a light-grey stipple (col(7,7), CP437 176) -- pale and obvious. A dark shaft sprite made level 61's 456-pit minefield invisible.

36.comment: Larger pentagram; the small one barely registered.

38.comment: Block, MBlock and ZBlock are all col(6,7) brown glyph 178 in the original -- indistinguishable, so which one a spell will break is not given away. MBlock reveals itself by moving.

43.comment: Block, MBlock and ZBlock are all col(6,7) brown glyph 178 in the original -- indistinguishable, so which one a spell will break is not given away.

52.comment: Drawn identically to Wall in the original (col(6,7), Wall glyph). The camouflage is the puzzle: only the matching OSpell reveals it.

53.comment: Drawn identically to Wall in the original (col(6,7), Wall glyph). The camouflage is the puzzle: only the matching OSpell reveals it.

54.comment: OWall3 is the one open wall the original tints grey, col(7,7).

64.comment: GBlock is col(7,7) grey, the one block the original sets apart.

65.comment: A single round boulder. Must read as pushable, not as wall texture: level 40 is 1192 of these.

66.comment: Electrified wall: col(12,0) bak(4,7), light red on red -- not cyan.

75.comment: A hanging chain, built from Castlevania.png by tools/make-rope.ts. Tiles vertically without a seam.

76.comment: Drawn as plain chain, same as a rope. A chord becomes rope the moment you touch it, so showing it as anything else broke the run visually. tools/make-sprites.ts still builds dropchord.png if a distinct sprite is wanted.

252.comment: The secret-message tree. Drawn exactly like a Tree in the original, so it stays hidden.

196.comment: CP437 196, the horizontal rule. Only four levels use it and always as a full 64-cell row; on the gravity levels it sits directly above the chandeliers, so it is drawn as the same chain rotated.

player.comment: An armoured adventurer. Teal is unused elsewhere in the palette, so the player stays readable against forest, brick, lava and stone.
